content:
The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

$ taproot get tooltip
# Tooltip

Use Tooltip to show the name of an icon-only control when a person points at it or focuses it.

A short text label that appears next to an icon-only control while a person points at it or focuses it, and disappears when they move away or dismiss it. Its text is the control's accessible name, so the label people see and the name assistive technology reads are the same.

## When to use

- Name an icon-only button, such as a trash icon that deletes a row or a pencil icon that edits it.
- Name each control in a toolbar of icon-only actions, where there is no room for text labels.

## When not to use

- Label a control that already shows its name as text. Instead: No tooltip. The visible text already names it. A tooltip repeats it and gets in the way of whatever sits next to the control.
- Name an icon that is not a control, such as a status symbol beside a value. Use [Icon](component.icon) instead. A tooltip only appears on something a person can focus. Give the icon a label, or state its meaning in text beside it.
- Explain the expected format of a form field, or why its value is invalid. Use [Text field](component.text-field) instead. The field's hint and error are always visible and are read with the field. A tooltip hides the information until someone goes looking for it.
- Explain why an action is disabled. Instead: A short text near the action. A disabled control cannot take focus, so keyboard users would never see a tooltip on it. Button's explain-disabled rule asks for visible text.
- Show content that has links, buttons, or more than a short phrase. Use [Dialog](component.dialog) instead. A tooltip cannot be interacted with and disappears when the pointer leaves. Content a person has to read or act on needs a surface they open on purpose.
- Give information that people must see to complete a task. Instead: Visible text on the page. Touch screens have no hover, and many people never point at a control before using it. A tooltip is only a reminder of what a control does.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| trigger | interactive-surface | The supplied icon-only control that the tooltip names, such as a Button. Tooltip does not draw it. |
| bubble | label | The floating text that names the trigger. It appears beside the trigger, above other content, and does not take focus. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | The text the bubble shows. It is also the trigger's accessible name, so the trigger needs no other name. Required. |
| placement | enum | `above`, `below` | `above` |  |

`placement` values:

- `above`: Shows the bubble above the trigger, or below it when there is no room above.
- `below`: Shows the bubble below the trigger, or above it when there is no room below.

## States

`default`, `open`

## Rules

### Content

- **SHOULD** label-short: Write the label as a few words that name the action or the object, with no ending punctuation. It is the control's name, so the same words a text button would use fit.
  - Do: Delete row; Edit profile
  - Avoid: Click here to delete this row from the table.; Trash

### Behavior

- **MUST** one-trigger: A tooltip names exactly one control, and that control is one a person can focus, such as a Button.
  - See: component.button#icon-accessible-name
- **MUST** opens-on-hover-and-focus: The bubble opens when the pointer rests on the trigger for a moment, and at once when the trigger receives keyboard focus.
- **MUST** closes-on-leave: The bubble closes when the pointer has left both the trigger and the bubble, when focus leaves the trigger, or when the trigger is activated.
- **MUST** not-interactive: The bubble never takes focus and holds no links, buttons, or other controls.
- **MUST** stays-in-view: The bubble appears above all other content and is not clipped by a scrolling container. When there is no room on the side set by placement, it moves to the opposite side, and it never runs past the edge of the viewport.
- **MUST** does-not-shift-layout: Opening the bubble does not move or resize anything on the page. The trigger keeps its own size and position.
- **SHOULD** one-open: Only one bubble is open at a time. Opening one closes any other.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** label-names-trigger: The label is the trigger's accessible name. Assistive technology reads it once, as the name of the control, and does not read the bubble as separate text.
- **MUST** stays-while-hovered: The bubble stays open while the pointer is on the trigger or on the bubble, so the pointer can move onto the bubble without it closing.
- **MUST** escape-closes: Escape closes the bubble without moving focus or changing anything else. It stays closed until the pointer or focus leaves the trigger and comes back.

## Accessibility

- Role: None of its own. The trigger keeps its role.
- Name: Gives the trigger its accessible name from the label parameter.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Escape | Close the bubble without moving focus. |

## Rationale

- **Tooltip names its trigger and has no description mode.** Naming icon-only controls is the need the system has now, and a label tooltip keeps what people see and what assistive technology reads the same. A tooltip that adds supplementary text to a control that already has a name is a separate decision, with its own reading order, so it waits for a real need.
- **The bubble uses the surface color with the default border and the popover elevation.** The system has no inverse surface role, and adding one is a token change, not part of adding a component. The default border keeps the bubble's edge visible on any surface and in forced-colors mode, where the shadow disappears and the border takes the system text color. semantic.elevation.md is the role the tokens name for popovers, so no new shadow token is needed.
- **Tooltip has one size and no density setting.** The bubble holds a few words in the small label style next to a control of any size. A larger bubble would only mean the label is too long.
- **Placement offers above and below only.** Above and below fit every trigger, including controls in a row, and they read the same in either text direction, so nothing mirrors. Start and end placements can come later without changing these two.
- **The bubble appears and disappears without animation.** The hover delay already keeps the bubble from flashing. With no motion there is nothing to reduce when the person prefers reduced motion.
- **Tooltip has no disabled, selected, loading, or invalid state.** Those belong to the trigger. A disabled control cannot take focus, so keyboard users would never see its tooltip, which is why the usage guidance sends that explanation to visible text.
- **Touch has no way to open the bubble.** Touch screens have no hover, and a long press is already used by the platform. The label still names the control for assistive technology. This is why a tooltip only names a control and never holds information a person needs.
- **The hover delay is fixed at about a third of a second and is not a token.** The delay keeps bubbles from flashing as the pointer crosses a toolbar. It is timing, not motion, and the motion duration tokens describe animations, so the value lives in the rules and the implementation.

## Links

### alternative

- [Dialog](component.dialog) — Show content that has links, buttons, or more than a short phrase. A tooltip cannot be interacted with and disappears when the pointer leaves. Content a person has to read or act on needs a surface they open on purpose.
- [Icon](component.icon) — Name an icon that is not a control, such as a status symbol beside a value. A tooltip only appears on something a person can focus. Give the icon a label, or state its meaning in text beside it.
- [Text field](component.text-field) — Explain the expected format of a form field, or why its value is invalid. The field's hint and error are always visible and are read with the field. A tooltip hides the information until someone goes looking for it.

### follows

- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

### related

- [Button](component.button)
- [Button](component.button#icon-accessible-name)

$ taproot get text-field --impl web
# Text field

Use Text field to collect a single line of text with a label, hint, and error.

Collects one line of text and associates a label, optional hint, and optional error with the control.

## When to use

- Collect a short value such as a name, email, or search query.
- Pair with Button when the value should be submitted.

## When not to use

- Collect multi-line text. Use [Text area](component.text-area) instead. Text field is a single line.
- Choose from a known set of options. Use [Select](component.select) instead. Text field does not present choices.
- Trigger an action by itself. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Text field collects a value.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | Label, control, hint, and error stacked together. |
| label | label | Visible name for the value. |
| control | interactive-surface | Single-line text control. |
| hint | description | Optional supporting guidance. |
| error | description | Optional message that says what to fix. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| error | string |  |  | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the control invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| type | enum | `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `url`, `tel` | `text` |  |
| name | string |  |  | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name. |
| value | string |  |  | Current value. The value given at creation is the initial value that reset restores. |
| placeholder | string |  |  | Example text shown when the value is empty. Not a replacement for the label. |
| autocomplete | string |  |  | Guidance for automatic filling from previously supplied information, such as email. |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Prevents editing. A disabled field does not submit its value. |
| required | boolean |  | `false` | The value must be provided before submit. Conveyed by more than color. |

`type` values:

- `text`: Plain single-line text.
- `email`: Email address.
- `password`: Concealed secret.
- `search`: Search query.
- `url`: Web address.
- `tel`: Telephone number.

## Events

- `input`: The value changed while editing.
- `change`: The value was committed.

## States

`disabled`, `invalid`, `hover`, `focus`, `default`

## Accessibility

- Role: Text input
- Name: Required from the visible label.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to or from the field. |
| Printable characters | Insert text. |

## Rationale

- **Text field consumes semantic tokens directly.** Tokens ADR 0003. Focus, invalid, disabled, surface, and text already have semantic roles. No component-token namespace.
- **Invalid is a state driven by the error message.** The message is the accessible signal. A variant axis would hide that the state comes from the error.
- **Label, hint, and error belong to the field.** A separate field shell does not exist yet. Association stays on this control until that shell lands.

## Links

### alternative

- [Button](component.button) — Trigger an action by itself. Text field collects a value.
- [Select](component.select) — Choose from a known set of options. Text field does not present choices.
- [Text area](component.text-area) — Collect multi-line text. Text field is a single line.

### alternative-to

- [Slider](component.slider) — Enter an exact number, or a number from a very large range. Typing is faster and more precise than dragging to one value among hundreds.
- [Text area](component.text-area) — Collect a short single-line value. Text field keeps short values compact.
- [Tooltip](component.tooltip) — Explain the expected format of a form field, or why its value is invalid. The field's hint and error are always visible and are read with the field. A tooltip hides the information until someone goes looking for it.

### follows

- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)
- [Form field](pattern.form-field)

### related

- [Badge](component.badge)
- [Checkbox](component.checkbox)
- [Select](component.select)
- [Slider](component.slider)
- [Text area](component.text-area)

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-text-field>`

### Import

```js
import { defineTextField } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/text-field";

defineTextField();
```

### Usage

```html
<form>
  <ds-text-field label="Email" name="email" type="email" hint="Used for sign-in." required></ds-text-field>
  <ds-button type="submit">Continue</ds-button>
</form>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | attribute | parameter `label` | string | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| `hint` | attribute | parameter `hint` | string | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| `error` | attribute | parameter `error` | string | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the control invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| `type` | attribute | parameter `type` | `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `url`, `tel` |  |
| `name` | attribute | parameter `name` | string | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name. |
| `value` | attribute | parameter `value` | string | Current value. The value given at creation is the initial value that reset restores. |
| `placeholder` | attribute | parameter `placeholder` | string | Example text shown when the value is empty. Not a replacement for the label. |
| `autocomplete` | attribute | parameter `autocomplete` | string | Guidance for automatic filling from previously supplied information, such as email. |
| `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean | Prevents editing. A disabled field does not submit its value. |
| `required` | attribute | parameter `required` | boolean | The value must be provided before submit. Conveyed by more than color. |
| `form` | property |  | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary. |
| `input` | event | event `input` |  | The value changed while editing. |
| `change` | event | event `change` |  | The value was committed. |

A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.

### Forms

Text field defaults to `type="text"`. Set `name` so the value is included when the form submits.
Pair it with Button to submit:

```html
<form>
  <ds-text-field label="Email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required></ds-text-field>
  <ds-button type="submit">Continue</ds-button>
</form>
```

A non-empty `error` marks the field invalid, associates that message with the control, and blocks
submit until the message is cleared. Use `hint` for guidance that is not an error.

To validate in your own code, set `novalidate` on the form so the submit reaches your listener.
Read the values there, and set `error` on each field that needs a correction. Clear `error` on the
field's `input` event and when the form resets, because a reset leaves it set.

The `value` attribute sets the initial value, which form reset restores. `autocomplete` takes the
HTML autofill tokens, such as `email` or `current-password`, so the browser can offer saved values.

### Styles

Install `@taproot-ds/tokens` alongside this package, and load its token stylesheet once at
the application root. Without it, the component has no colors, spacing, or type.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
```

Without a bundler, link the package's `dist/css/tokens.css` instead.

$ taproot get pattern.form-field
# Form field

Give every form control the same label, hint, error, required, disabled, and form behavior.

Text field, Text area, Select, Checkbox, Switch, and Radio group share the guidance below. Each
component record keeps only the rules about its own control, such as what its value is.

## Label

Provide a visible label that names the value. The label is the control's accessible name.
Placeholder text is not a label. Write "Email address", not "Enter email".

## Hint

Use a hint for format, purpose, or consequence that the label does not already state. The hint is
associated with the control, so assistive technology reads it as the description.

## Error

Write the error as what to fix: "Enter an email address with an @ sign", not "Invalid".

- A non-empty error marks the control invalid, and clearing the error removes that state.
- Clear the error when the person edits the value. A form reset restores the value but leaves the
  error, so clear it on reset too.
- While a non-empty error is set, the control blocks its form from submitting.
- The error is associated with the control, so assistive technology reads it as the description.
- The invalid state always includes the text message. Meaning never depends on color alone.

## Required

A required control is announced as required, and shows it by more than color. A required control
with no value blocks its form from submitting.

## Disabled

Disabled prevents interaction from pointer and keyboard, and a disabled control submits nothing.
When the reason a control is unavailable is not obvious, explain it nearby.

## Form value

Inside a form, the control's value submits under its name, and reset restores the initial value.
Each component says what its value is, such as the checked option of a Radio group.

## Focus

Keyboard focus stays visible in every state, including under forced colors.

## Switch and forms

Switch applies its setting immediately, without a separate submit action. It can also submit with a
form, so the guidance on this page applies to it. Use Checkbox when the choice takes effect only
when the form is submitted.

## Links

### followed-by

- [Checkbox](component.checkbox)
- [Radio group](component.radio-group)
- [Select](component.select)
- [Slider](component.slider)
- [Switch](component.switch)
- [Text area](component.text-area)
- [Text field](component.text-field)

No, a tooltip isn't right here. Put the password format in the `hint` of **Text field**, using `type="password"`.

**Why not Tooltip**
- Taproot's Tooltip only names icon-only controls. Its "When not to use" list includes "Explain the expected format of a form field, or why its value is invalid" and points to Text field instead.
- People need the format to complete the task, but a tooltip hides it until someone goes looking. Touch screens have no hover, so those users would never see it.
- Tooltip has no description mode. Its label becomes the trigger's accessible name (`component.tooltip#label-names-trigger`, MUST), so it would also replace the name of whatever it's attached to.

**What to use instead**
- **`hint`:** this holds the format rules. It's always visible and is read as the field's accessible description, and `pattern.form-field` names format as a use for it.
- **`error`:** this says what to fix when a value fails, such as "Add at least one number" rather than "Invalid". Clear it when the person edits the value and when the form resets, because a non-empty error blocks submit.
- **`placeholder`:** don't put the format here, because it's only example text shown while the field is empty.

```html
<ds-text-field
  label="Password"
  name="password"
  type="password"
  autocomplete="new-password"
  hint="At least 12 characters, including a number and a symbol."
  required
></ds-text-field>
```

That's the web component version, and the hint text is only an example, so swap in your actual rules. `autocomplete="new-password"` suits a sign-up or change-password form; use `current-password` on sign-in.
